category_title: Students with learning disabilities exhibiting low motivation, poor frustration tolerance, and resistance to academic demands
minimal_context: The student is completing a 15-minute independent warm-up worksheet in a secondary inclusive classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start your 15-minute independent warm-up activity on the worksheet covering yesterday's material.

STUDENT: (Sits with eyes and head not oriented towards the independent seatwork assignment) I don't remember how to do this.

TUTOR: Just look at the first question and see what you can do.

STUDENT: It's too hard. I don't get the content at all.

TUTOR: Keep trying, you still have time left to finish.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet away, not holding a pencil or responding to questions in written form) I'm not doing it. I'm just going to sit here.

options.A: Maintain a ratio of praise statements to error correction statements ranging from 3:1 or 5:1 to 10:1 during the independent warm-up.
options.B: Make a list of activities for the day at the beginning of the session and tape the class schedule to the student's desk.
options.C: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student regarding the independent warm-up worksheet instead of imposing control.
options.D: Remind the student, walk by their desk more frequently, and make a class announcement right before the independent warm-up begins.
